risikabel.explanation: "Risikabel" means "risky", with a real chance that something goes wrong or is lost. Use it for a choice or plan: "en risikabel plan" (a risky plan). For something that can hurt you, say "farlig" (dangerous): "en farlig hund" (a dangerous dog).

sentence.da: Det er en **risikabel** plan, for vi kan miste alle pengene.
sentence.en: It is a risky plan, because we could lose all the money.

ro.explanation: "Ro" means "calm" and "peace and quiet": "Jeg vil gerne have ro" (I would like some peace and quiet). To tell someone to relax, say "Slap af" (Relax).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have **ro**, når jeg læser.
sentence.en: I would like some peace and quiet when I read.

robust.explanation: "Robust" means "robust", able to take hard use without breaking or getting ill: "en robust cykel" (a sturdy bike). For a person, it means not getting sick or upset easily: "Hun er robust" (She is tough).

sentence.da: Telefonen er **robust**, så den kan tåle et fald.
sentence.en: The phone is robust, so it can survive a fall.

rock.explanation: "Rock" means "rock" as in music. The stone is "en sten" (a stone), not rock.

sentence.da: Jeg elsker **rock** med høje guitarer og trommer.
sentence.en: I love rock with loud guitars and drums.

rodet.explanation: "Rodet" means "messy", for a room or desk with things lying around. It is not about dirt: "Rummet er rodet, men ikke snavset" (The room is messy, but not dirty).

sentence.da: Børneværelset er meget **rodet** i dag.
sentence.en: The children's room is very messy today.

rolig.explanation: "Rolig" means "calm" or "relaxed", and "peaceful" or "quiet" for places. "Vær rolig" means "Stay calm" or "Calm down". The form "roligt" means "calmly": "Tal roligt" (Speak calmly).

sentence.da: Peter er helt **rolig** og smiler.
sentence.en: Peter is completely calm and smiling.

romantik.explanation: "Romantik" means "romance", the feeling of love and closeness between two people: "Der er ikke meget romantik i at vaske op" (There is not much romance in doing the dishes).

sentence.da: Levende lys og blomster giver **romantik**.
sentence.en: Candles and flowers bring romance.

romantisk.explanation: "Romantisk" means "romantic", for love and dreamy moments, such as "en romantisk aften" (a romantic evening) or "en romantisk gave" (a romantic gift).

sentence.da: Det er **romantisk** at gå en tur ved havet.
sentence.en: It is romantic to go for a walk by the sea.

roning.explanation: "Roning" means "rowing", the sport of moving a boat forward with oars and your own muscle power.

forms.en: to do rowing (as a club sport)

sentence.da: Til **roning** bruger man årer og sin egen muskelkraft.
sentence.en: For rowing you use oars and your own muscle power.

ros.explanation: "Ros" means "praise", words that tell someone they did well. You get it with "at få" (to get): "at få ros" (to get praise).

sentence.da: Hun fik meget **ros** for sit arbejde.
sentence.en: She got a lot of praise for her work.

rug.explanation: "En rug" means "rye", a cereal crop grown for its flour. Danes use it above all for the dark bread called "rugbrød" (rye bread).

sentence.da: Mel af **rug** gør brødet mørkt og tungt.
sentence.en: Flour made from rye makes the bread dark and heavy.

rugbrød.explanation: "Rugbrød" means "rye bread", a dark, heavy bread. It is made of rug (rye) and brød (bread). It is the bread under most "smørrebrød" (open sandwiches).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger ost på en skive **rugbrød**.
sentence.en: I put cheese on a slice of rye bread.

rummelig.explanation: "Rummelig" means "spacious", with a lot of room inside: "en rummelig bil" (a spacious car). It is built on et rum (a room, a space).

sentence.da: Bilen er **rummelig**, og der er plads til hele familien.
sentence.en: The car is spacious, and there is room for the whole family.

rund.explanation: "Rund" means "round", for a shape. It is also used for round numbers: "runde tal" (round numbers) are numbers like 10 and 100.

sentence.da: Jorden er **rund**, ikke flad.
sentence.en: The earth is round, not flat.

rundt om hjørnet.explanation: "Rundt om hjørnet" means "around the corner". It can be a place: "Posthuset ligger rundt om hjørnet" (The post office is around the corner). It can also be a time: "Julen er lige rundt om hjørnet" (Christmas is just around the corner).

forms.en: The bakery is around the corner.

forms.da: Butikken er lige rundt om hjørnet.
forms.en: The shop is just around the corner.

sentence.da: Banken ligger lige **rundt om hjørnet**.
sentence.en: The bank is just around the corner.

rusland.explanation: "Rusland" means "Russia". Use "i" (in) for being there and "til" (to) for going there: "Jeg bor i Rusland" (I live in Russia), "Jeg rejser til Rusland" (I am traveling to Russia).

sentence.da: Man taler russisk i **Rusland**.
sentence.en: People speak Russian in Russia.

russisk.explanation: "Russisk" means "Russian", for the language and for things from Russia. Danish writes languages and nationalities with a lowercase letter, so "russisk" is not capitalized.

sentence.da: Han kommer fra Rusland og taler **russisk**.
sentence.en: He comes from Russia and speaks Russian.

ryddelig.explanation: "Ryddelig" means "tidy", with everything in its place: "Værelset er ryddeligt" (The room is tidy). The action is "at rydde op" (to tidy up).

sentence.da: Hendes lejlighed er altid **ryddelig** og pæn.
sentence.en: Her apartment is always tidy and nice.

rynket.explanation: "Rynket" means "wrinkled", with small folds or lines in a surface, for skin and clothes. It comes from "at rynke" (to wrinkle): "at rynke panden" is to frown (literally, to wrinkle the forehead).

sentence.da: Skjorten er helt **rynket**, så jeg må stryge den.
sentence.en: The shirt is all wrinkled, so I have to iron it.

rystende.explanation: "Rystende" means "shocking": so upsetting that it shakes you. It comes from "at ryste" (to shake), and it is used for literal shaking as well: "rystende hænder" (trembling hands).

sentence.da: Billederne fra ulykken var **rystende**, og mange græd.
sentence.en: The pictures from the accident were shocking, and many cried.

rystet.explanation: "Rystet" means "shaken", deeply troubled after a shock such as an accident or bad news: "Jeg er stadig rystet efter ulykken" (I am still shaken after the accident). It comes from "at ryste" (to shake).

sentence.da: Hun var meget **rystet** efter den alvorlige ulykke på motorvejen.
sentence.en: She was very shaken after the serious accident on the highway.

rå.explanation: "Rå" means "raw" for food. For words and behavior it means "crude" or "rough": "et råt sprog" (rough language).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke lide **rå** løg.
sentence.en: I do not like raw onions.

rædselsslagen.explanation: "Rædselsslagen" means "terrified", very strongly afraid. It is built from en rædsel (a horror) and slagen (struck), so it is literally "struck by horror". It is much stronger than "bange" (afraid).

sentence.da: Hun blev **rædselsslagen**, da hun så slangen på gulvet.
sentence.en: She became terrified when she saw the snake on the floor.

rød.explanation: "Rød" means "red". It is part of words like "rødvin" (red wine) and "rødbede" (beet).

sentence.da: Tomaten er **rød**.
sentence.en: The tomato is red.

rødgrød.explanation: "En rødgrød" means "red berry pudding", a thick dessert of cooked red berries, eaten cold with cream. Despite the ending "grød" (porridge), it has no grain in it: it is thickened berry juice.

forms.en: a bowl of red berry pudding

sentence.da: Til dessert fik vi kold **rødgrød** med fløde.
sentence.en: For dessert we had cold red berry pudding with cream.

rødhåret.explanation: "Rødhåret" means "red-haired", with red or ginger hair. Many hair words are built the same way, from a color or a quality plus "hår" (hair): "lyshåret" (fair-haired), "mørkhåret" (dark-haired), "gråhåret" (gray-haired).

sentence.da: Min lillesøster er **rødhåret**, og hendes hår er næsten orange.
sentence.en: My little sister is red-haired, and her hair is almost orange.

røg.explanation: "Røg" means "smoke", the gray cloud that comes from burning things, such as a cigarette.

forms.en: There is smoke in the room.

sentence.da: Jeg kan se **røg** fra skorstenen.
sentence.en: I can see smoke from the chimney.

rørende.explanation: "Rørende" means "touching" or "moving", which makes you feel warm or tearful. It comes from "at røre" (to touch, to stir). How you feel is "rørt" (moved): "Jeg blev rørt" (I was moved).

sentence.da: Talen var **rørende**, og flere i salen græd.
sentence.en: The speech was touching, and several people in the hall cried.

rørsukker.explanation: "Rørsukker" means "cane sugar", sugar made from sugarcane. The first part, "rør", means "reed", and the same word is in "sukkerrør" (sugarcane).

sentence.da: **Rørsukker** laves af planten sukkerrør, som vokser i varme lande.
sentence.en: Cane sugar is made from the plant sugarcane, which grows in warm countries.

rørt.explanation: "Rørt" means "touched" and describes being moved by a warm or sad moment: "Jeg blev rørt over hendes ord" (I was touched by her words). It is not about touching something with your hand.

sentence.da: Jeg blev så **rørt** over din gave.
sentence.en: I was so touched by your gift.

røræg.explanation: "Røræg" means "scrambled eggs". It comes from "at røre" (to stir) and "æg" (egg), because you stir the eggs while they cook. Eggs fried whole are "spejlæg" (fried eggs).

sentence.da: Vi laver **røræg** med bacon til morgenmad.
sentence.en: We make scrambled eggs with bacon for breakfast.

at sagsøge.explanation: "At sagsøge" means "to sue", to take a person or a company to court to demand money or a ruling. The one who sues is called "sagsøgeren" (the plaintiff).

sentence.da: Hun vil **sagsøge** firmaet, fordi det ikke betalte hende.
sentence.en: She wants to sue the firm because it did not pay her.

at samarbejde.explanation: "At samarbejde" means "to cooperate", built from sam (together) and arbejde (work). To name the person you cooperate with, add "med" (with) before that person: "Jeg samarbejder med naboen" (I cooperate with the neighbor).

sentence.da: Vi skal **samarbejde** for at løse opgaven.
sentence.en: We have to work together to solve the task.

at samle.explanation: "At samle" means "to gather" or "to collect": "Læreren samler børnene" (The teacher gathers the children). For a hobby, add "på" (on): "Jeg samler på frimærker" (I collect stamps). It can also mean to put together: "Jeg samler en reol" (I am putting together a bookcase).

sentence.da: Min bror vil **samle** på gamle mønter.
sentence.en: My brother wants to collect old coins.

at samle på.explanation: "At samle på" means "to collect" as a hobby, like stamps or coins. Without "på" (on), "at samle" means "to gather" or "to pick up": "Hun samler blomster" (She picks flowers).

sentence.da: Min søn vil **samle på** frimærker.
sentence.en: My son wants to collect stamps.

at sammenfatte.explanation: "At sammenfatte" means "to summarize", to gather the main points of a long text or talk into a short form: "sammenfatte rapporten" (to summarize the report).

sentence.da: Kan du **sammenfatte** mødet i tre linjer?
sentence.en: Can you summarize the meeting in three lines?

at sammenkalde.explanation: "At sammenkalde" means "to convene", to call people together for a meeting. It is used when someone with authority, such as a boss, a board or a government, makes the call: "sammenkalde et møde" (to call a meeting).

sentence.da: Formanden vil **sammenkalde** bestyrelsen til et møde i morgen.
sentence.en: The chairman will convene the board for a meeting tomorrow.

at sammenligne.explanation: "At sammenligne" means "to compare" and is used with "med" (with): "Jeg sammenligner prisen med prisen i går" (I compare the price with yesterday's price). It is built from sammen (together) and ligne (to look like).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sammenligne** priserne i to butikker.
sentence.en: I want to compare the prices in two stores.

at sammensætte.explanation: "At sammensætte" means "to put together", to join separate parts, such as a team, a menu or a piece of furniture. A word made of two words is "et sammensat ord" (a compound word).

sentence.da: Træneren skal **sammensætte** et hold til næste kamp.
sentence.en: The coach has to put together a team for the next match.

at sanse.explanation: "At sanse" means "to sense", to notice something through your eyes, ears, nose, skin or tongue. It is also used for noticing a mood without being told: "Hun sanser, at han er nervøs" (She senses that he is nervous).

sentence.da: Hun kan **sanse**, når nogen er ked af det.
sentence.en: She can sense when someone is sad.

at satse.explanation: "At satse" means "to bet" and "to go for". With "på" (on), it means to put your hope or effort on one choice: "Hun satser på en karriere som musiker" (She is going for a career as a musician). To put money on a game or race is also "at satse": "Han satsede hundrede kroner på hesten" (He bet a hundred kroner on the horse).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **satse** på en uddannelse i stedet for et job.
sentence.en: I want to go for an education instead of a job.

at savne.explanation: "At savne" means "to miss" someone or something that is not here. It is not used for a missed bus. For that, Danes say "Jeg nåede ikke bussen" (I did not catch the bus).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **savne** min familie meget.
sentence.en: I will miss my family a lot.

at scanne.explanation: "At scanne" means "to scan", either to copy a paper into a computer or to read a barcode with a phone camera.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **scanne** brevet og sende det.
sentence.en: I want to scan the letter and send it.

at score.explanation: "At score" means "to score" in sports, when a player puts the ball in the net or over the line.

sentence.da: Han vil **score** et mål i kampen.
sentence.en: He wants to score a goal in the match.

at scrolle.explanation: "At scrolle" means "to scroll", to move up or down a page on a screen. To name the direction, add "ned" (down) or "op" (up): "scrolle ned" (scroll down), "scrolle op" (scroll up).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **scrolle** i timevis på min telefon.
sentence.en: I can scroll for hours on my phone.

at se.explanation: "At se" means "to see", and also "to watch": "Jeg ser en film" (I am watching a movie). "Jeg kan se, hvad du mener" (I can see what you mean). "Vi ses!" (See you!) "At kigge" (to look) is for looking on purpose: "Kig her!" (Look here!).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **se** dit hus fra her.
sentence.en: I can see your house from here.

at se bort fra.explanation: "At se bort fra" means "to disregard", to not let something count when you decide: "Hvis vi ser bort fra prisen, er det en god bil" (If we disregard the price, it is a good car). "Bort" means "away", so it is like looking away from it.

sentence.da: Du kan ikke bare **se bort fra** reglerne.
sentence.en: You cannot just disregard the rules.

at se efter.explanation: "At se efter" means "to look for" and "to check". To look out for something: "Jeg ser efter bussen" (I am looking out for the bus). To check that something is as it should be: "Se efter, om døren er låst" (Check whether the door is locked).

sentence.da: Kan du **se efter** mine nøgler?
sentence.en: Can you look for my keys?

at se frem til.explanation: "At se frem til" means "to look forward to". It is common at the end of a letter: "Jeg ser frem til at høre fra dig" (I look forward to hearing from you).

sentence.da: Børnene kan **se frem til** en lang sommerferie.
sentence.en: The children can look forward to a long summer break.

at se ned på.explanation: "At se ned på" means "to look down on", to think a person is worth less than you. It also works for looking down from a high place: "Jeg ser ned på gaden" (I look down at the street). The opposite is "at se op til" (to look up to).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **se ned på** folk, bare fordi de er fattige.
sentence.en: You must not look down on people just because they are poor.

at se op til.explanation: "At se op til" means "to look up to", to think highly of someone and want to be like them.

sentence.da: Børn har ofte brug for nogen at **se op til**.
sentence.en: Children often need someone to look up to.

at se på.explanation: "At se på" means "to look at", with your eyes on something: "Hun ser på billedet" (She looks at the picture). Do not mix it up with "at lede efter" (to look for): "Jeg leder efter min nøgle" (I am looking for my key).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **se på** billedet.
sentence.en: I want to look at the picture.

at se tilbage.explanation: "At se tilbage" means "to look back", with your eyes or in your memory. For looking back at the past, add "på" (on): "se tilbage på sommeren" (look back on the summer).

sentence.da: Hun vil **se tilbage** på sin barndom.
sentence.en: She wants to look back on her childhood.

at se tv.explanation: "At se tv" means "to watch TV". Danish uses "se" (to see) where English says "watch", as in "se en film" (to watch a movie). "At se fjernsyn" (to watch television) means the same. "Tv" is said as two letters, "te-ve".

sentence.da: Vi vil **se tv** i aften.
sentence.en: We want to watch TV tonight.

at se ud.explanation: "At se ud" means "to look", in the sense of how something appears: "Du ser træt ud" (You look tired). "Hvordan ser det ud?" (What does it look like?) Looking at something with your eyes is "at se på" (to look at).

sentence.da: Min bror skal **se ud** som en pirat til festen.
sentence.en: My brother has to look like a pirate at the party.

at sejle.explanation: "At sejle" means "to sail", and it covers any trip on water, with or without sails, even by engine. Rowing is a different word, "at ro" (to row).

sentence.da: Om sommeren vil vi **sejle** til en lille ø.
sentence.en: In the summer, we want to sail to a small island.

at sende.explanation: "At sende" means "to send", for example a letter, a parcel or an email. You can put the person right after the verb: "Jeg sender dig en besked" (I send you a message). Or you can name the person after the item with "til" (to): "Jeg sender en besked til dig" (I send a message to you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sende** et brev til mor.
sentence.en: I want to send a letter to Mom.

at sende en sms.explanation: "At sende en sms" means "to text", or literally to send an SMS. To indicate who receives the text, use "dig" (you) or a name: "Jeg sender dig en sms" (I send you a text).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sende en sms** til min ven.
sentence.en: I want to send a text to my friend.

at servere.explanation: "At servere" means "to serve" food or drinks, for example in a restaurant or for guests at home.

sentence.da: Tjeneren vil **servere** maden nu.
sentence.en: The waiter will serve the food now.

at shoppe.explanation: "At shoppe" means "to shop", mostly for fun, like looking for clothes. For groceries, use "at købe ind" (to buy groceries): "Jeg køber ind til aftensmad" (I am buying groceries for dinner).

sentence.da: Vi skal **shoppe** i byen i weekenden.
sentence.en: We are going shopping in town this weekend.

at sidde.explanation: "At sidde" means "to sit", the state of already being in a chair. For sitting next to something, use "ved" (at): "Jeg sidder ved computeren" (I am sitting at the computer). To sit down is "at sætte sig" (literally, to put oneself).

sentence.da: Du kan **sidde** på stolen.
sentence.en: You can sit on the chair.

at sidde fast.explanation: "At sidde fast" means "to be stuck", the state of not moving: "Bilen sidder fast" (The car is stuck). You also say it when you cannot go on: "Jeg sidder fast med opgaven" (I am stuck on the task).

sentence.da: Lastbilen kan **sidde fast** i mudderet.
sentence.en: The truck can end up stuck in the mud.

at sige.explanation: "At sige" means "to say": "Hvad siger du?" (What are you saying?) To tell a story, use "at fortælle" (to tell) instead: "Hun fortæller en historie" (She tells a story).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **sige** tak.
sentence.en: The children must say thank you.

at sige farvel.explanation: "At sige farvel" means "to say goodbye". Among friends, Danes often say "hej hej" (bye bye) or "vi ses" (see you) instead of "farvel" (goodbye).

sentence.da: Vi skal **sige farvel** til vores gæster.
sentence.en: We have to say goodbye to our guests.

at sige goddag.explanation: "At sige goddag" means "to say hello", literally to say good day. Like "good day" in English, "goddag" sounds formal or old-fashioned. With friends, you would normally say "hej" (hi).

sentence.da: Du skal **sige goddag** til min mor.
sentence.en: You must say hello to my mother.

at sige op.explanation: "At sige op" means "to quit" or "to resign": "Han sagde op i går" (He quit yesterday). It is also used to cancel something, such as a subscription: "Jeg sagde mit abonnement op" (I canceled my subscription).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sige op** og finde et nyt job.
sentence.en: I want to quit and find a new job.

at sige til.explanation: "At sige til" means "to tell" or "to let someone know", so that they can act: "Sig til, hvis du har brug for hjælp" (Tell me if you need help). Without "til" (to), "at sige" only means "to say": "Hun sagde hej" (She said hi).

sentence.da: Du skal **sige til**, når du er sulten.
sentence.en: You have to let me know when you are hungry.

at sige undskyld.explanation: "At sige undskyld" means "to say sorry". "Undskyld" alone also gets someone's attention: "Undskyld, ved du, hvor stationen er?" (Excuse me, do you know where the station is?)

sentence.da: Du skal **sige undskyld** til din bror.
sentence.en: You have to say sorry to your brother.

at signere.explanation: "At signere" means "to sign". For a form or contract, Danes more often say "at skrive under" (to sign a paper). "Signere" is common for autographs and for players or artists who sign with a club or label: "Spilleren har signeret med klubben" (The player has signed with the club).

sentence.da: Forfatteren vil **signere** bøger i boghandlen på lørdag.
sentence.en: The author will sign books in the bookstore on Saturday.

at sigte.explanation: "At sigte" means "to aim" and "to charge". To aim is to point at something you want to hit: "Han sigter på dåsen" (He aims at the can). To charge is when the police say officially that someone is suspected of a crime: "Han er sigtet for tyveri" (He is charged with theft).

sentence.da: Skytten skal **sigte**, før hun trykker på aftrækkeren.
sentence.en: The shooter has to aim before she pulls the trigger.

at sikre.explanation: "At sikre" means "to secure" and "to ensure": to fasten or guard something so it cannot get hurt or lost, or to make sure it happens. For example, "Vi sikrer, at alle får mad" (We make sure everyone gets food). Do not mix it up with "at forsikre" (to insure): "Jeg forsikrer bilen" (I insure the car).

sentence.da: Du skal **sikre** lasten med stropper, så den ikke falder af.
sentence.en: You must secure the load with straps so that it does not fall off.

at simulere.explanation: "At simulere" means "to simulate", to copy a real situation, usually on a computer, to try it out or practice it. It can also mean to fake: "Han simulerer sygdom" (He is faking an illness).

sentence.da: Piloterne kan **simulere** en nødlanding i en flysimulator.
sentence.en: The pilots can simulate an emergency landing in a flight simulator.

at sjuske.explanation: "At sjuske" means "to be sloppy", to do a task carelessly and too fast, so the work is not done well. To name the task you do carelessly, add "med" (with) before the task: "sjuske med lektierne" (to be sloppy with the homework).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **sjuske**, når du skriver en vigtig mail.
sentence.en: You must not be sloppy when you write an important email.

at skabe.explanation: "At skabe" means "to create", to bring something new into being, such as new jobs: "skabe nye job" (create new jobs). For everyday making, use "at lave" (to make): "lave mad" (make food).

sentence.da: Vi vil **skabe** en ny hjemmeside sammen.
sentence.en: We want to create a new website together.

at skabe sig.explanation: "At skabe sig" means "to make a fuss", to act in an over-the-top way, often to get attention: "Han skaber sig" (He is making a fuss). It looks like "at skabe" (to create), but the word "sig" (oneself) changes the meaning completely.

sentence.da: Han kan **skabe sig**, når han ikke får sin vilje.
sentence.en: He can make a fuss when he does not get his way.

at skade.explanation: "At skade" means "to harm" or "to damage": "Det skader ikke" (It does no harm). "Regnen skadede huset" (The rain damaged the house). To hurt yourself, add "sig" (oneself): "Jeg skadede mig" (I hurt myself).

sentence.da: For meget sukker kan **skade** dine tænder.
sentence.en: Too much sugar can harm your teeth.

at skaffe.explanation: "At skaffe" means "to get" or "to obtain", often with some effort: "Kan du skaffe mad til alle?" (Can you get food for everyone?) Just receiving something is "at få" (to get): "Jeg fik en gave" (I got a gift).

sentence.da: Vi kan **skaffe** billetter til dig.
sentence.en: We can get tickets for you.

at skamme sig.explanation: "At skamme sig" means "to be ashamed", to feel bad because you did something wrong or foolish. To tell someone they ought to be ashamed, say "Skam dig!" (Shame on you!).

sentence.da: Man skal ikke **skamme sig** over at bede om hjælp.
sentence.en: You should not be ashamed of asking for help.

at skele.explanation: "At skele" means "to be cross-eyed", to have eyes that do not point the same way. With "til" (at) it means "to glance", often with interest or envy: "Han skeler til naboens bil" (He eyes the neighbor's car).

sentence.da: Drengen skal have briller, fordi han kan **skele**.
sentence.en: The boy needs glasses because he can be cross-eyed.

at skelne.explanation: "At skelne" means "to distinguish", to see or hear that two things are not the same: "Jeg kan ikke skelne mellem tvillingerne" (I cannot tell the twins apart). It is only about noticing, not about taking things apart, which is "at adskille" (to separate).

sentence.da: Farveblinde kan have svært ved at **skelne** rød fra grøn.
sentence.en: Colorblind people can have trouble telling red from green.

at skifte.explanation: "At skifte" means "to change" by swapping one thing for another: "Jeg skifter dæk" (I change tires). To make something become different, use "at ændre" (to change): "Jeg ændrer planen" (I am changing the plan).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skifte** tøj, når vi kommer hjem.
sentence.en: I want to change clothes when we get home.

at skifte mening.explanation: "At skifte mening" means "to change one's mind": "Hun skiftede mening og blev hjemme" (She changed her mind and stayed home). For a thing, like a shirt, use plain "skifte" (change): "skifte skjorte" (change a shirt).

sentence.da: Du kan **skifte mening**, når du vil.
sentence.en: You can change your mind whenever you want.

at skifte tøj.explanation: "At skifte tøj" means "to change clothes". The verb "at skifte" (to change) also works with other things: "skifte job" (to change jobs).

sentence.da: Jeg er våd og vil **skifte tøj**.
sentence.en: I am wet and want to change clothes.

at skifte ud.explanation: "At skifte ud" means "to replace": you swap an old thing for a new one. "Ud" (out) comes after the old thing you take away: "Jeg skifter pæren ud" (I replace the light bulb). In sports it means to substitute a player, taking one out and putting another in.

sentence.da: Træneren vil **skifte ud** midt i kampen.
sentence.en: The coach wants to substitute in the middle of the game.

at skildre.explanation: "At skildre" means "to depict", to show a person, a place or an event in words or pictures, in a book, a film or a painting.

sentence.da: Maleren vil **skildre** havnen i et stort maleri.
sentence.en: The painter wants to depict the harbor in a large painting.

at skille.explanation: "At skille" means "to separate", to pull two things apart: "Jeg skiller sort tøj fra hvidt" (I separate black clothes from white). It is also used for divorce: "De blev skilt" (They got divorced).

sentence.da: Du skal **skille** æggeblommen fra hviden.
sentence.en: You have to separate the yolk from the white.

at skilles.explanation: "At skilles" means "to separate", and for a couple "to divorce". It also means parting ways: "Vi skilles ved stationen" (We part at the station).

sentence.da: Mine forældre vil **skilles**, men de er venner.
sentence.en: My parents want to get divorced, but they are friends.

at skinne.explanation: "At skinne" means "to shine", like the sun or a lamp. It also works for people who look happy: "Hun skinner af glæde" (She glows with joy).

sentence.da: Solen vil **skinne** hele weekenden.
sentence.en: The sun will shine all weekend.

at skjule.explanation: "At skjule" means "to hide", so others cannot see or find something. It also works for feelings: "Hun skjuler sin vrede" (She is hiding her anger).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skjule** pakken under sengen.
sentence.en: I will hide the package under the bed.

at skrabe.explanation: "At skrabe" means "to scrape", to pull a hard edge across a surface to remove something from it: "Han skrabede malingen af væggen" (He scraped the paint off the wall). Danes also use it for carrots: "at skrabe gulerødder" (to peel carrots).

sentence.da: Jeg må **skrabe** isen af forruden, før jeg kan køre.
sentence.en: I have to scrape the ice off the windshield before I can drive.

at skraldgrine.explanation: "At skraldgrine" means "to roar with laughter", to laugh very loudly at something funny. It is much stronger than "at grine" (to laugh). To name what made you laugh, add "af" (at) before it: "Vi skraldgrinede af filmen" (We roared with laughter at the movie).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **skraldgrine**, når klovnen falder i vandet.
sentence.en: The children will roar with laughter when the clown falls into the water.

at skrige.explanation: "At skrige" means "to scream", often from fear, pain or anger: "Hun skreg af smerte" (She screamed in pain). For loud but normal calling, use "at råbe" (to shout).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **skrige** højt, når jeg er bange.
sentence.en: I can scream loudly when I am scared.

at skrive.explanation: "At skrive" means "to write". It also covers typing and texting: "skrive en besked" (to write a message).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skrive** et brev til mor.
sentence.en: I want to write a letter to Mom.

at skrive af.explanation: "At skrive af" means "to copy", to write out text that someone else wrote. At school it means to cheat by copying a neighbor's answers: "Han skrev af efter sin nabo" (He copied from his neighbor).

sentence.da: Munkene plejede at **skrive af** gamle bøger i hånden.
sentence.en: The monks used to copy old books by hand.

at skrive ned.explanation: "At skrive ned" means "to write down", to keep something on paper so you remember it: "Skriv det ned, så du ikke glemmer det" (Write it down so you do not forget it).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skrive ned**, hvad han siger.
sentence.en: I want to write down what he says.

at skrive til.explanation: "At skrive til" means "to write to" a person, with "til" (to) naming the person who receives the writing. The same phrase is used for texting: "Skriv til mig!" (Text me!)

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skrive til** min lærer i dag.
sentence.en: I want to write to my teacher today.

at skrubbe.explanation: "At skrubbe" means "to scrub", to clean something by pressing and moving a stiff brush over it. "Skrub af!" (Get lost!) is a rude way to tell someone to leave.

sentence.da: Jeg skal **skrubbe** gulvet, fordi det er blevet meget beskidt.
sentence.en: I have to scrub the floor because it has gotten very dirty.

at skrue.explanation: "At skrue" means "to screw", to turn a screw in or out: "Han skruer låget af" (He unscrews the lid). With "op" (up) or "ned" (down), it means to turn something up or down, and "for" (for) comes before the thing you turn: "Skru ned for musikken" (Turn down the music).

sentence.da: Kan du **skrue** hylden fast på væggen?
sentence.en: Can you screw the shelf onto the wall?

at skrælle.explanation: "At skrælle" means "to peel", such as potatoes, carrots and fruit. The skin you take off is "en skræl" (a peel).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **skrælle** fem kartofler.
sentence.en: I have to peel five potatoes.

at skræmme.explanation: "At skræmme" means "to scare": "Du skræmte mig!" (You scared me!) To be scared yourself, say "at være bange" (to be afraid): "Jeg er bange for edderkopper" (I am scared of spiders).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **skræmme** katten.
sentence.en: You must not scare the cat.
